channel.description: Interactive, reproducible scientific visualization with canvasXpress — in R, Python and JavaScript.

item.title: Interactive volcano plots in JavaScript with CanvasXpress
item.dc:creator: Isaac Neuhaus
item.description:
A volcano plot puts log fold change on x, statistical significance on y, and pushes the interesting genes into the top corners. CanvasXpress is a JavaScript library at heart, so in the browser there’s no wrapper at all — you give a <canvas> a data object and a config, and you get an interactive, reproducible figure. The same spec renders identically from R and Python too.

Load the library

Drop one script tag (and the stylesheet) on your page. Here we pin to a released version on a CDN:

<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>

The markup and the spec

Give the page a canvas, then build the data (a value matrix plus annotations) and a config, and call new CanvasXpress(...):

<canvas id="volcano" width="650" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
  // Normal-distribution helpers (no stats library needed in the browser)
  function gauss() {                        // standard normal via Box–Muller
    var u = 0, v = 0;
    while (u === 0) u = Math.random();
    while (v === 0) v = Math.random();
    return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v);
  }
  function normCdf(x) {                      // standard normal CDF via an erf approximation
    var s = x < 0 ? -1 : 1, ax = Math.abs(x) / Math.SQRT2;
    var t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * ax);
    var y = 1 - (((((1.061405429 * t - 1.453152027) * t + 1.421413741) * t - 0.284496736) * t + 0.254829592) * t) * Math.exp(-ax * ax);
    return 0.5 * (1 + s * y);
  }

  // Simulate a realistic volcano: most genes unchanged, a minority differentially
  // expressed; significance follows effect size / standard error. Genes are the
  // variables (rows); each row holds [logFC, -log-pVal].
  var genes = [], rows = [], group = [], fc = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
    var de = Math.random() < 0.12;                          // ~12% truly changed
    var sgn = Math.random() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1;
    var effect = de ? sgn * (0.8 + 0.9 * Math.random()) : 0;
    var se = 0.22 + 0.5 * Math.random();                    // per-gene standard error
    var f = effect + se * gauss();                          // observed log2FC
    var praw = 2 * (1 - normCdf(Math.abs(f / se)));         // z-test p-value
    var p = Math.min(-Math.log(Math.max(praw, 1e-16)) / Math.LN10, 16);
    genes.push("Gene" + (i + 1));
    rows.push([Math.round(f * 1000) / 1000, Math.round(p * 1000) / 1000]);
    group.push(f > 1 && p > 1.3 ? "Increased" : f < -1 && p > 1.3 ? "Decreased" : "NoChange");
    fc.push(Math.round(Math.pow(2, Math.abs(f)) * 100) / 100);
  }

  var data = {
    y: { vars: genes, smps: ["logFC", "-log-pVal"], data: rows },
    z: { Group: group, FC: fc }
  };

  var config = {
    graphType: "Scatter2D",
    title: "Publication-ready volcano plot",
    xAxis: ["logFC"], yAxis: ["-log-pVal"],
    xAxisTitle: "log2 fold change", yAxisTitle: "-log10 p-value",
    colorBy: "Group",
    colorKey: { Group: { Increased: "rgba(197,27,38,0.75)",
                         Decreased: "rgba(33,102,172,0.75)",
                         NoChange:  "rgba(150,150,150,0.35)" } },
    sizeBy: "FC", sizes: [3, 6, 9, 12, 15],
    showDecorations: true,
    decorations: { line: [
      { color: "rgba(120,120,120,0.8)", width: 1, x: 1 },
      { color: "rgba(120,120,120,0.8)", width: 1, x: -1 },
      { color: "rgba(120,120,120,0.8)", width: 1, y: 1.301 }
    ] }
  };

  new CanvasXpress("volcano", data, config);
</script>

Live result

Here’s exactly that code, running on this page:

Hover a point for its gene and values, drag to zoom, or use the toolbar to filter by regulation group. The dashed guides mark the ±1 log2FC and p = 0.05 cutoffs.

Why “reproducible”

The data and config above are the figure — one portable JSON specification. Save it and the identical plot renders from the R (canvasXpress) and Python (canvasxpress) packages, and it can be validated against a published schema and re-rendered later, so a figure can be regenerated and audited rather than just viewed.

  • Source & npm: https://github.com/neuhausi/canvasXpress

item.title: Kaplan–Meier survival curves in JavaScript with CanvasXpress
item.dc:creator: Isaac Neuhaus
item.description:
Kaplan–Meier curves summarize time-to-event data: the step-down survival probability over time, usually split by a group like treatment arm. CanvasXpress computes the survival steps for you — you give it a time column and a censoring column — so in the browser it’s just a data object and a config. The result is interactive and reproducible.

Load the library

<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>

The markup and the spec

Subjects are the variables (rows); each row holds [Time, Time-Censor] (1 = censored, 0 = event). The arm rides along as a variable annotation. The key is graphType: "KaplanMeier" and passing both columns to xAxis.

<canvas id="km" width="650" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
  var subj = [], rows = [], arm = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
    var a = Math.random() < 0.5 ? "Treatment" : "Control";
    var base = a === "Treatment" ? 60 : 40;                 // treatment survives longer
    var time = Math.round(-base * Math.log(Math.random()) * 10) / 10;  // exponential
    var cens = Math.random() < 0.3 ? 1 : 0;                 // 1 = censored, 0 = event
    subj.push("Subj" + (i + 1));
    rows.push([time, cens]);
    arm.push(a);
  }

  var data = {
    y: { vars: subj, smps: ["Time", "Time-Censor"], data: rows },
    z: { Arm: arm }
  };

  var config = {
    graphType: "KaplanMeier",
    xAxis: ["Time", "Time-Censor"],
    colorBy: "Arm",
    title: "Overall survival by treatment arm",
    xAxisTitle: "Time (weeks)", yAxisTitle: "Probability of survival",
    invertCensored: true,                 // draw censoring ticks
    showKMConfidenceIntervals: false
  };

  new CanvasXpress("km", data, config);
</script>

Live result

Hover any step for the time and survival probability; the tick marks are censored subjects. CanvasXpress derives the survival curve from the raw table, so you never precompute the steps — and the same spec re-renders the identical curve from R or Python.

A common gotcha

The survival transform only fires with graphType: "KaplanMeier". A bare "Scatter2D" gives a raw scatter of the censor values instead — survival probability is computed by the engine, not a column in your data.

  • Source & npm: https://github.com/neuhausi/canvasXpress

item.title: Clustered heatmaps in JavaScript with CanvasXpress
item.dc:creator: Isaac Neuhaus
item.description:
The clustered heatmap is the default way to look at an expression matrix: rows and columns reordered by similarity, dendrograms on the margins, and sample metadata alongside. CanvasXpress clusters inside the render, so in the browser you pass a plain matrix and get an interactive, reproducible figure.

Load the library

<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>

The markup and the spec

Genes are the variables (rows), samples the columns; the matrix goes in as data, and the sample annotation becomes a track over the columns. samplesClustered / variablesClustered turn on hierarchical clustering with dendrograms.

<canvas id="heatmap" width="650" height="550"></canvas>
<script>
  // standard normal via Box–Muller
  function gauss() {
    var u = 0, v = 0;
    while (u === 0) u = Math.random();
    while (v === 0) v = Math.random();
    return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v);
  }

  var ng = 40, ns = 30, genes = [], samps = [], cond = [], matrix = [];
  for (var j = 0; j < ns; j++) { samps.push("S" + (j + 1)); cond.push(j < ns / 2 ? "Tumor" : "Normal"); }
  for (var i = 0; i < ng; i++) {
    genes.push("Gene" + (i + 1));
    var row = [];
    for (var k = 0; k < ns; k++) {
      var val = gauss();
      if (i < 20 && cond[k] === "Tumor")   val += 2;        // first block up in Tumor
      if (i >= 20 && cond[k] === "Normal") val += 2;        // second block up in Normal
      row.push(Math.round(val * 1000) / 1000);
    }
    matrix.push(row);
  }

  var data = {
    y: { vars: genes, smps: samps, data: matrix },
    x: { Condition: cond }
  };

  var config = {
    graphType: "Heatmap",
    samplesClustered: true, variablesClustered: true,
    colorSpectrum: ["navy", "white", "firebrick3"],
    showSmpDendrogram: true, showVarDendrogram: true,
    title: "Clustered expression heatmap"
  };

  new CanvasXpress("heatmap", data, config);
</script>

Live result

Rows and columns are reordered by similarity, the dendrograms show the clustering, and the samples separate cleanly by condition. Hover a cell for its gene, sample and value; the whole figure is one portable spec you can store, validate and re-render from R or Python.
